newsitem.title: INDIA: India lifts bonus ceiling for post, phone workers.
newsitem.headline: India lifts bonus ceiling for post, phone workers.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Tuesday removed a ceiling on bonus payments for postal and telephone workers on strike for the past seven days, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Indian Telecommunications Minister Beni Prasad Varma announced the decision on the key issue, which prompted the strike, after a cabinet meeting, the news agency said.
About one million postal and telephone workers in India went on strike against a government decision of a 3,500 rupees ($100) ceiling on annual pay bonuses.
Millions of letters have piled up as a result of the strike by six trade unions, three of them representing postal unions.
Telephone workers have stopped manual services like repairs and billing in telephone exchanges but most telephones are working because of automated exchanges.
The government's decision on Tuesday to lift the ceiling on bonus payment is expected to pave way for an end to the seven-day old strike, the United News of India (UNI) said.
